Four screens, one question.

Is this water open, and what is it doing right now? Everything on the left is live — real reaches, real regulations, five gauges against a century of record, and real stocking releases.

A GAUGE HAS A LIMIT

The Fraser at Hope drains 216,600 km². It knows nothing about a creek above Chilliwack.

So every reach is scored on the ratio of its FWA stream magnitude to the gauge's. Above 0.1 the station is describing your water; below 0.001 it is not, and the reach goes back to grey dotted no matter how neatly it nests. That rule alone takes the Fraser gauge from claiming 601 reaches to —.

FLOW IS A PERCENTILE

15.7 m³/s means nothing on its own. The 4th percentile for 30 August against 97 years means something.

Every station carries a day-of-year envelope built from its whole record, so the colour on the map is standing, not magnitude. All five here are below their 10th percentile.

SPOTS ARE A LOG, NOT A BOOKMARK

Pin an exact point on a stream and the app writes down what the water and the sky were doing when you were there.

Gauge reading and its standing, air temperature, wind, rain over the previous three days, the regulation in force that day — then your own notes and photographs on top.
